warning_texts: This profile is single-vendor. Every context in this run is one Claude Opus model family: architect, workers, auditors and this red team. The chain of LLM PASS verdicts is therefore not independent review, and a mistake the model is prone to would be repeated on both sides of every check.

What actually holds in this run is the deterministic layer: the machine gates, the frozen check_plan, the control lock and the release surface gate. This verdict does not replace it, and no GPT or other cross-vendor gate over the work exists in this system.

Write access to the raw sources and frozen machinery was closed by permissions.deny in .claude/settings.json for the edit tools only, not for the shell, and permissions.allow is no barrier at all. A modified raw file would have been caught by the control lock after the fact, not prevented, and I did

The LLM stage results carry no verifiable work. Every worker result, gate0_semantic and gate_release_auditor cite one check whose value, 0.473684, occurs nowhere in this dataset, and gate0_semantic's evidence is a one-line stub.

The metrics and claims auditors say they 'recomputed independently from' the registry they audit, so their checks are circular. In this run the only independent checks were the machine gates and this red team.

Every worker and auditor result.json and every carry is stamped 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. That is before the analysis plan's registered_at of 2026-04-02 and months before this run was dispatched on 2026-09-19, so these timestamps were not read from a clock and cannot order events.

No worker result has a disclosures field, all worker warnings are empty, and the results' artifacts list only the src/ scripts, not the data they wrote. No stage reported a deviation, command or tool refusal, so there was nothing to assess for effect on the numbers.

The client's fifth question (R05, the quarter's shipping cost) is missing from the release. report.md and dashboard_data.json never mention shipping, so a reader cannot tell the question was asked or why it is unanswered.

The reason R05 is unanswered appears only in analysis/answers/R05.json: 2,648 of 44,531 orders (5.95%) have a blank, NaN or inf shipping cell, which counts as zero, so the unpublished shipping_total of 37,792,722.50 understates itself by an unknown amount.

shipping_total reproduces at 37,792,722.50 EUR under the declared locale, but that is 12.5 times the quarter's net revenue and about 902 EUR per readable order against an average order value near 100 EUR. The column's unit or scale needs a business check before this metric is ever published; strippi

Both registered tests show p as 0.0000 on report.md and dashboard_data.json, and the registry stores 0.0000000000. The recomputed p is about 2.9e-157 for completion and below double precision for AOV, so a reader sees a p of zero where 'p < 0.0001' is what the data support.

The completion rate is a snapshot of the export: 3,457 direct orders (14.05%) and 4,034 partner orders (20.24%) were still pending and count as not completed. The published gap of 0.1197 would be 0.0578 if every pending order delivered, and 0.0847 among resolved orders only.

The report's caveats say the interval is sampling-only, but not that pending orders sit in the completion denominator as non-completions. The plan's assumption that neither channel changed how it books orders during the quarter cannot be checked from this export.

Of the human decisions, dedup_rule is the one the data can least confirm. Where the two revisions' updated_at differs (368 repeats), the last row is always the later one. In 549 of the 917 repeats both revisions share one updated_at, so file order alone decides, and 6 of those change status.

If the first revision won instead of the last, net_revenue would be 3,010,704.83 (12,591.78 lower), completion would be 0.722161 for direct and 0.601184 for partner, and the order count would not change. All 126 status changes between revisions run from pending or cancelled to delivered, including 6

Net revenue is ordered value net of refunds on delivered orders, not cash received. It excludes shipping, and it excludes 7,491 pending orders worth 800,300.55 net that may still deliver after the export. The caveat 'delivered orders only' implies this but does not size it.

The release surface gate binds all 60 numbers across the three files in release/, with no [:N] slice, no magnitude filter and no UNVERIFIED_CLAIM marker. Its evidence does not list the generator-literal scan of src/release/build_release.py, and src/ is outside my inputs, so 'no business literal in t

The release gate's text_exclusions keep three reader-visible numbers out of it: the period label, 'n = N' and '0.95 interval'. I checked them myself: the four n equal my recounts of 24,597, 19,934, 17,818 and 12,055, and 0.95 equals the plan's level. No machine rule binds them.

Some places had no deterministic rule, and my reading was their only check. They are report prose and population statements, dashboard fields other than numbers, carry contents, and the renamed customer_id, order_date and country columns together with the derived is_delivered and shipping_missing fl
I could not read raw_data/questions.md, which is outside my inputs. That the client asked exactly R01 to R05, and in these words, rests on gate_claims_machine questions_are_answered alone.
The handoff carries no drift_since_review. That shows only that no stage code was flagged as reviewed on another export, not that the code's assumptions are proven on this one.
The AOV test's effect size, 0.4869, is Cohen's d on the pooled standard deviation. On the average of the two variances it would be 0.4950, and the analysis plan does not name the convention.
summary: FAIL on six blockers, none of them in the numbers. My own code recomputed every published figure from the quarantine projection, and all 60 rendered numbers on the three release surfaces agree exactly with it. Two blockers are on the release. First, report.md tells the reader the whole document is delivered-only, although the 44,531 orders include 7,167 cancelled and 7,491 pending and the completion rates divide by all of them. Second, the dashboard's four estimate cards show both bounds but neither n nor the 0.95 level. The other four blockers are the worker carries. All four are one template
